Review.Independence: The same agent that wrote review 1, which took no part in authoring or implementing the change or its fixes and saw nothing of those conversations. This pass covers the complete diff a3d2b7d..32540c6 (80 files): everything read for review 1 at 12cb717, plus the whole of the fix commit 12cb717..32540c6 read line by line (src/state.ts, src/records.ts, the four command files, the conformance helper, the new review-gaps.test.ts, and the seven changed documents). review-1.xml as committed is byte-identical to the file I wrote. Given this time, beyond the skill's hand-over: the author's list of what each fix claims to do; every claim was checked against the code and by rerunning probes, none was taken on trust. All four automated checks were rerun at 32540c6 and exited 0 (53 tests pass, 1 skipped); the log hashes of run-3 match its receipt. Probes: 5 groups, about 30 invocations, in throwaway repositories under the OS temp directory; 11 mutations of the fixed code in a throwaway clone. Limits unchanged from review 1: the approval statement was not compared with its conversation; K1 rests on the targeted search of review 1, and the fix commit adds no file and no passage that would reopen it; the interrupted-receipt path cannot be exercised on Windows; CK5 is the owner's and has no observation; packages/** and cli-reference.md are covered by the byte comparison of CK4, the HTML style blocks were not read. K5 has no rule file and no Rule element; it is upheld, with the residue in F13.

Finding.Text: Review 1: step 5 of close failed open when git could not resolve the start revision; a shallow clone closed a change that wrote a protected path.
Finding.Resolution: evaluate now sets startUnresolved when the diff cannot be computed and close refuses. Rerun: in a `git clone --depth 1`, status prints `next: start revision cannot be resolved` and close exits 1 with that phrase, for a change that wrote a protected path and for one that did not. Removing the condition turns test RV-01 red. The order in which it is reported is F15.

Finding.Text: Review 1: close did not verify what the review covered; start-revision, end-revision and contract-sha256 of the review were never used.
Finding.Resolution: reviewObligation now compares all three. Rerun: start-revision equal to HEAD is refused (review does not cover the complete diff); an end-revision that does not exist or that carries another candidate is refused (review covers an earlier candidate); a wrong contract hash is refused (review covers an earlier revision); an end-revision one records-only commit behind HEAD is accepted, as it should be. Each of the three conditions, removed alone, turns RV-02 red.

Finding.Text: Review 1: a blocking finding marked owner-disposed closed without an OwnerDecision.
Finding.Resolution: readReview reads OwnerDecision and close refuses without it. Rerun: `blocking finding F1 is disposed without an owner decision`; a blank element is rejected by the schema; with the element present the change closes. Removing the condition turns RV-03 red. The schema still leaves the element optional and a finding marked resolved needs no Resolution; neither is required by evidence-records.md.

Finding.Text: Review 1: packages/**, src/tools, the help form and --version were present and absent from the surface table of method.md.
Finding.Resolution: The table now names packages/ under Skills, a row for the tools of this repository under src/tools/, and --help and --version under Commands. Read in the diff and compared with the tree: nothing present is unlisted except the word form `grace5 help` (F16).

Finding.Text: Review 1: refusals were printed on standard output although commands.md says standard error.
Finding.Resolution: close, run, status and init now print `refused:` with console.error. Rerun: every refusal in the probes arrived on stderr with stdout empty; RV-07 asserts the stream and fails when close is put back on stdout.

Finding.Text: Unchanged and kept by the author as designed: a file under .grace5/changes/ that a check command executes, or code placed there, is outside the candidate and the dirty state, and can change after a pass without voiding it. Unlike F7, no document states this limit; source-identity.md still argues only from the definition hash.
Review 1: skip-worktree and ignored files let a receipt say dirty="false" for a tree the candidate does not describe, and the document did not name the limit.
Finding.Resolution: source-identity.md now states that what git is told to ignore or assume unchanged is invisible to the kernel and is the project's responsibility. Read in the diff; the behaviour is unchanged by decision. The separate remark that a failing `git status` reads as a clean tree is carried in F16.

Finding.Text: Review 1: defects reported by check did not hold run or close.
Finding.Resolution: Every defect except an unused check is now an obligation of step 1, and run refuses on it for an approved revision. Rerun: a brief omitting a protected path and an approval with a duplicate stale Bound each refuse start and close with `change has defects: ...`; a change with an unused check still runs and closes. Removing the close condition turns RV-04 red. The run condition has no test (F16).

Finding.Text: Unchanged and kept by the author as designed: a change counts as closed when a file named close.xml exists, valid or not, and status does not compare a close record with the state it names.
Review 1: no test for rule violated, definition changed, review of another revision, an unbound check or a result recorded dirty; loose refusal assertions.
Finding.Resolution: review-gaps.test.ts adds nine tests with exact phrases and closing controls. My judgement, as asked: the edit does only what evidence-records.md says this repository does with run logs, it is not a test of an affected file, and it is acceptable as it stands; it stays on the record as an unlisted write that a Path element would have covered.

Finding.Text: Unchanged, left for judgement: init.ts carries its own copy of the ChangeId pattern, contract.ts and records.ts restate schema defaults, and the model is read by a second hand-written XML reader that fails closed where it could disagree with xmllint. My judgement: none of this is a second copy of the validation rules in the sense K5 forbids, and it is acceptable; the pattern in init.ts is the one piece that could drift from common.xsd unnoticed.
Review 1: .grace5/README.md said the kernel did not exist; retirement.md left G-12 unchecked; smaller observations on a killed rerun, two provenance lines and the hand-written start run.
Finding.Resolution: The README sentence is replaced and G-12 is checked with a reference to this review. Read in the diff. G-12 now rests on a targeted search, which is less than its column heading claims (F16). The other observations describe behaviour the documents allow and are unchanged.

Finding.Text: New, introduced by the fix for F1. evidence-records.md now makes resolvability of the start revision part of step 3 (a start run exists and its source revision can be resolved), before step 4 (no dirty source path). The kernel tests it after step 4, under the comment for step 5. Probe: in a shallow clone with one untracked source file, close answers `working tree is dirty`, although the earlier unmet step is step 3. The document says close refuses at the first unmet step and K3 binds the order, so this is a violation of the cited rule, narrow as it is: the change is still refused, and either the line in evaluate or the sentence in step 3 can move. No test puts the two conditions together.

New, smaller. The help text of close in cli.ts, and so the generated cli-reference.md, still lists steps 1, 3 and 8 in their wording before the fix; it no longer says what close verifies. The phrase `approval does not bind check` can no longer be reached, because any missing or wrong Bound is first a defect of check; commands.md still lists it and RV-09 accepts either phrase. run refuses on defects only while the revision is approved for execution, which is narrower than the sentence added to commands.md, and removing that refusal leaves the whole suite at 53 pass. The new tests are named RV-01 to RV-09 and do not carry the ids FS-15 to FS-18 they serve. `grace5 help` still works as a word and the table lists only --help. dirtyPaths still returns an empty list when git status fails. retirement.md marks G-12 verified absent on the strength of a targeted search.

Review.Adequacy: Unchanged from review 1: `tsc --noEmit` separates a tree that type-checks from one that does not, a failure of A1 that CK2 cannot see because Bun runs TypeScript unchecked. It discriminates that failure mode and no other; the behavioural part of A1 rests on CK2. A narrow check that shares its criterion; read alone against A1 it would not discriminate.

`bun test` now runs 54 black-box tests. For A2 a pass discriminates: every case of conformance.md, FS-15 to FS-18 included, has a test, and across both passes 23 of 24 mutations that made the kernel accept a case or drop a refusal turned the test of that case red; the survivor is the run refusal on defects. For A1 it reaches the close obligations review 1 found untested. It does not reach the order of steps 3 and 4 (F15), and on Windows one test is skipped, so the pass of run-3 does not include the interrupted receipt.

Review.Rule: K1. The verdict of review 1 stands: one shared file name with unrelated content, and none of some sixty distinctive lines, headings and identifiers found in the GRACE 4 repository. The fix commit adds one test file written against this kernel's own phrases and edits existing files; nothing in it resembles GRACE 4 material. A targeted search, not a proof. No deferred proposal is implemented.

K2. The surface table now lists the packages, the repository tools, --help and --version, and everything it lists exists. No deferred proposal is implemented. The unlisted word form of help is noted in F16 and does not change the verdict.

K3. Every refusal the file states is now issued, with one fixed phrase each: the gaps of review 1 (F1, F2, F3, F8) are closed and were reprobed. The order is followed for steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 as probed in both passes. It is not followed for the second half of step 3: an unresolvable start revision is reported after the dirty tree of step 4 (F15).
K4. Every mechanism the kernel implements maps to one of L-01 to L-21, the mechanisms added by the fix fall under L-13, L-15 and L-16, and every entry now states a removal criterion.
